parts.passageHtml:
{[A.][245632]} {[Traditionally uniforms were — and for some industries still are — manufactured to protect the worker.][245633]} {[ When they were first designed, it is also likely that all uniforms made  symbolic sense - those for the military, for example, were originally intended to impress and even terrify the enemy; other uniforms denoted a hierarchy - chefs wore white because they worked with flour, but the main chef wore a black hat to show he supervised.][245648]}

{[B.][245704]} {[The last 30 years, however, have seen an increasing emphasis on their role in projecting the image of an organization and in uniting the workforce into a homogeneous unit — particularly in “customer facing" industries, and especially in financial services and retailing.][245706]} {[From uniforms and workwear has emerged ‘corporate clothing’.][245745]} {["The people you employ are your ambassadors," says Peter Griffin, managing director of a major retailer in the UK.][245754]} {["What they say, how they look, and how they behave is terribly important. "][245773]} {[The result is a new way of looking at corporate workwear.][245787]} {[From being a simple means of identifying who is a member of staff, the uniform is emerging as a new channel of marketing communication.][245798]}

{[C. Truly effective marketing through visual cues such as uniforms is a subtle art, however.][245821]} {[Wittingly or unwittingly, how we look sends all sorts of powerful subliminal messages to other people.][245836]} {[Dark colors give an aura of authority while lighter pastel shades suggest approachability.][245852]} {[Certain dress styles create a sense of conservatism, others a sense of openness to new ideas.][245866]} {[Neatness can suggest efficiency but, if it is overdone, it can spill over and indicate an obsession with power.][245881]} {[ "If the company is selling quality, then it must have quality uniforms.][245901]} {[If it is selling style, its uniforms must be stylish.][245912]} {[If it wants to appear innovative, everybody can’t look exactly the same.][245923]} {[Subliminally we see all these things," says Lynn Elvy, a director of image consultants House of Colour.][245936]}

{[D. But translating corporate philosophies into the right mix of color, style, degree of branding and uniformity can be a fraught process.][245954]} {[And it is not always successful.][245974]} {[According to Company Clothing magazine, there are 1000 companies supplying the workwear and corporate clothing market.][245981]} {[Of these, 22 account for 85% of total sales - £380 million in 1994.][245997]}

{[E. A successful uniform needs to balance two key sets of needs.][246014]} {[On the one hand, no uniform will work if staff feel uncomfortable or ugly.][246025]} {[Giving the wearers a choice has become a key element in the way corporate clothing is introduced and managed.][246039]} {[On the other hand, it is pointless if the look doesn’t express the business’s marketing strategy.][246057]} {[The greatest challenge in this respect is time.][246074]} {[When it comes to human perceptions, first impressions count.][246083]} {[Customers will size up the way staff look in just a few seconds, and that few seconds will color their attitudes from then on.][246093]} {[Those few seconds can be so important that big companies are prepared to invest years, and millions of pounds, getting them right.][246117]}

{[F. In addition, some uniform companies also offer rental services.][246141]} {["There will be an increasing specialization in the marketplace," predicts Mr Blyth, Customer Services Manager of a large UK bank.][246151]} {[The past two or three years have seen consolidation.][246170]} {[Increasingly, the big suppliers are becoming ‘managing agents’, which means they offer a total service to put together the whole complex operation of a company’s corporate clothing package - which includes reliable sourcing, managing the inventory, budget control and distribution to either central locations or to each staff member individually.][246180]} {[ Huge investments have been made in new systems, information technology and amassing quality assurance accreditations.][246211]}

{[G. Corporate clothing does have potential for further growth.][246228]} {[Some banks have yet to introduce a full corporate look; police forces are researching a completely new look for the 21st century.][246237]} {[And many employees now welcome a company wardrobe.][246247]} {[A recent survey of staff found that 90 per cent welcomed having clothing which reflected the corporate identity.][246255]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 6:

The passage First Impressions Count has seven paragraphs A-G. Which paragraphs discuss the following points?

Example:

The number of companies supplying the corporate clothing market

 Answer: D

questions.explanationHtml:
1

Đoạn F (The past two or three years have seen consolidation. Increasingly, the big suppliers are becoming ‘managing agents’, which means they offer a total service to put together the whole complex operation of a company’s corporate clothing package - which includes reliable sourcing, managing the inventory, budget control and distribution to either central locations or to each staff member individually)

F (các “purchasing agreement” hợp đồng mua bán rất đa dạng gồm “rental service”; “a total service” )

2

Đoạn A (Traditionally uniforms were — and for some industries still are — manufactured to protect the worker. When they were first designed, it is also likely that all uniforms made symbolic sense - those for the military, for example, were originally intended to impress and even terrify the enemy; other uniforms denoted a hierarchy - chefs wore white because they worked with flour, but the main chef wore a black hat to show he supervised.)

A (mục đích đầu tiên “original purpose” của “uniforms” đồng phục là để bảo vệ người đi làm, tạo nét đặc trưng, và đe doạ kẻ thù)

questions.text: The popularity rating of staff uniforms
questions.explanationHtml:
3

Đoạn G (A recent survey of staff found that 90 per cent welcomed having clothing which reflected the corporate identity.)

G (“the popularity rating” tỉ lệ phổ biến của đồng phục lên đến 90% nhân viên nghĩ rằng đồng phục tạo nên bản sắc của công ty)

questions.text: Involving employees in the selection of a uniform
questions.explanationHtml:
4

Đoạn E (Giving the wearers a choice has become a key element in the way corporate clothing is introduced and managed)

E (cho phép người mặc “wearers” = “employees” nhân viên quyền lựa chọn trong việc làm đồng phục)

questions.text: The changing significance of company uniforms
questions.explanationHtml:
5

Đoạn B (The last 30 years, however, have seen an increasing emphasis on their role in projecting the image of an organization and in uniting the workforce into a homogeneous unit — particularly in “customer facing" industries, and especially in financial services and retailing. From uniforms and workwear has emerged ‘corporate clothing’)

B (sự thay đổi lớn “the changing significance” về đồng phục công ty là nhấn mạnh vào tuyên truyền hình ảnh công ty “projecting the image of an organization” và thống nhất lực lượng lao động “uniting the workforce”)

questions.text: Perceptions of different types of dress
questions.explanationHtml:
6

 

 

Đoạn C (Dark colors give an aura of authority while lighter pastel shades suggest approachability. Certain dress styles create a sense of conservatism, others a sense of openness to new ideas. Neatness can suggest efficiency but, if it is overdone, it can spill over and indicate an obsession with power)

C (mỗi kiểu áo truyền đạt một quan niệm khác nhau:  áo màu tối → quyền lực; áo màu sáng → dễ tiếp cận; kiểu thể hiện sự bảo thủ, và kiểu áo thể hiện sự cởi mở)

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 7 - 13:

Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer of the passage? 

YES               if the statement agrees with the writer’s views
NO                 if the statement contradicts the writer’s views
NOT GIVEN   if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this

questions.text: Uniforms were more carefully made in the past than they are today.
questions.explanationHtml:
7

Không có đề cập thông tin so sánh giữa đồng phục hiện đại và ngày xưa

NG

questions.text: Uniforms make employees feel part of a team.
questions.explanationHtml:
8

Đoạn B (The last 30 years, however, have seen an increasing emphasis on their role in projecting the image of an organization and in uniting the workforce into a homogeneous unit)

Y (uniting a workforce” đoàn kết mọi người trong lực lượng lao động” thành 1 khối thống nhất “homogeneous unit” → khiến cho nhân viên cảm thấy mình là 1 phần của team “a part of the team”)

questions.text: Using uniforms as a marketing tool requires great care.
questions.explanationHtml:
9

Đoạn C (Truly effective marketing through visual cues such as uniforms is a subtle art, however. Wittingly or unwittingly, how we look sends all sorts of powerful subliminal messages to other people)

Y (marketing thông qua đồng phục đòi hỏi “great care” sự chú ý kĩ lưỡng, chi tiết vì “how we look” vẻ bề ngoài luôn gửi đi những thông điệp “messages”gì đó đến mọi người)

questions.text: Dressing too smart could have a negative impact on customers.
questions.explanationHtml:
10

Đoạn C (Neatness can suggest efficiency but, if it is overdone, it can spill over and indicate an obsession with power)

Y (“Too smart” ở đây nói về cách ăn mặc , có nghĩa là nhìn sang trọng, gọn gàng. Trong bài có thông tin “neatness” là sự ngăn nắp gọn gàng nhưng nếu bị “overdone” làm quá thì có thể có tác dụng tiêu cực là “obsession with power” sự ám ảnh quyền lực)

questions.text: Most businesses that supply company clothing are successful.
questions.explanationHtml:
11

Đoạn D (According to Company Clothing magazine, there are 1000 companies supplying the workwear and corporate clothing market. Of these, 22 account for 85% of total sales - £380 million in 1994)

N (có 1000 công ty cung cấp đồng phục nhưng 22 trong số đó chiếm 85% tổng doanh số → đa phần các công ty còn lại chiếm doanh số rất thấp nghĩa là không thành công → trái ngược hoàn toàn ý của câu hỏi là “most companies” thành công

questions.text: Uniforms are best selected by marketing consultants.
questions.explanationHtml:
12

Đoạn D (But translating corporate philosophies into the right mix of color, style, degree of branding and uniformity can be a fraught process. And it is not always successful.)

NG (người ta chỉ nói việc chuyển hoá từ triết lí của công ty sang màu sắc, phong cách đồng phục rất khó, KHÔNG ĐỀ CẬP đến việc ai sẽ là người chọn đồng phục)

questions.text: Clothing companies are planning to offer financial services in the future.
questions.explanationHtml:
13

Đoạn F (In addition, some uniform companies also offer rental services….  Increasingly, the big suppliers are becoming ‘managing agents’, which means they offer a total service to put together the whole complex operation of a company’s corporate clothing package - which includes reliable sourcing, managing the inventory, budget control and distribution to either central locations or to each staff member individually)

N (các công ty quần áo chỉ “offer” dịch vụ thuê “rental service” và “a total service” là dịch vụ tổng thiết kế quần áo theo gói cho cả tập đoàn chứ không phải là dịch vụ tài chính “financial service”
